commands.name: convert
commands.description:
Read a table from SOURCE and write it to TARGET; report both sides.

Options both sides have take --in- (the source) or --out- (the target).
--query is SQL over the source whose result is written: inside a base
it names its tables, over any other source the table is data.
With --dry-run the report comes back and nothing is written.
A TARGET that is the SOURCE itself, or a sheet with rows of a Google
spreadsheet that the write replaces, asks first: --confirm skips the question.
An address of many sources (a mask, a folder, a list) is read as one table:
--source-column names the column with the source of each row, --strict makes
different columns fail with SCHEMA_MISMATCH. A TARGET with {column} or {n} splits
the table (--split-by, --chunk-rows, --drop-split-column). A batch reports its
targets; --keep-going goes on after a failure and lists the errors (exit 1).
Sources that would be written to one target (a/x.csv, b/x.csv for {stem}) are refused first.
The action of SCHEMA_MISMATCH and TARGET_EXISTS names the flag to change (--strict, --mode).
--columns lists the source columns the target keeps, in this order; --rename
gives kept columns new names as old=new (the selection comes first). Both take a
comma list and repeat; a wrong name or a clash is INVALID_ARGUMENTS (exit 2).
--start and --value-input place and pass the values in a sheet of a service.
SOURCE - is stdin, its format comes from the content; TARGET - is stdout:
CSV, one value per line for one column, or --out-format; under --json the
data is inside the envelope as data.

Example: dataio convert a.csv b.csv --json

commands.name: info
commands.description:
Describe a source: format, encoding, delimiter, rows, column types, the first 5 rows, the sheets or tables.

With --query it describes the result of the SQL: inside a base it names
its tables, over any other source the table is data. A Google spreadsheet
lists its sheets; an address of many sources is described as the merged table
(--source-column, --strict, which fails with SCHEMA_MISMATCH); --credentials is the key file to reach it with.

Example: dataio info a.csv --json

commands.name: join
commands.description:
Join the columns of lookups to a main SOURCE by key columns and write it to TARGET.

--lookup is the address of a lookup and repeats; --on names a key column, or
main_name=lookup_name when the lookup calls it differently, and repeats for several keys.
--how keeps every source row (left, the default), every lookup row (right, one
lookup), the matched rows (inner) or all (full). Keys compare as text with outer
spaces trimmed; an empty key matches nothing. A lookup column whose name the table
has gets the suffix of the lookup. The report lists each lookup's rows, matched,
unmatched and empty keys. The --in- options are of every source, the --out- options
and the others of the target, as in convert. With --dry-run the report comes back and
nothing is written. A TARGET that is the SOURCE or a lookup, or a sheet with rows of a
Google spreadsheet that the write replaces, asks first: --confirm skips the question.
TARGET - is stdout, as in convert; under --json the data is inside the envelope as data.

Example: dataio join main.csv out.xlsx --lookup prices.xlsx#Prices --on sku --on region --how left

options.name: --lookup
options.description: Address of a lookup joined to the source, e.g. prices.xlsx#Prices; repeatable, joined in order.

options.name: --on
options.description: Key column: a name, or main_name=lookup_name; repeat for several keys.

options.name: --how
options.description: Rows kept: left every source row, right every lookup row (one lookup), inner the matched, full all.

commands.description:
Print this CLI's machine-readable contract: an OpenCLI document (opencli.org).

Commands, options, arguments, exit codes, plus `x-rb-*` metadata: env vars,

document on one line (no {"ok": ...} envelope); without, the same indented.

Example: dataio describe --json

commands.name: status
commands.description:
Report every provider's credential: where it comes from and whether it works. Never prints values.

Without --check only presence is reported (status `unchecked` or `missing`).
Exits 0 when every required provider is ok/unchecked (an optional one may be
missing), 3 when any required provider has a problem or any credential is
invalid/expired, 2 on a usage error. A per-target provider (one credential per
site/host/account) gets one entry per stored target, named `<kind>:<target>`. The --json shape is a cross-tool contract:
`tool`, `version`, `checked_at`, `credentials[]` with `provider`, `required`,
`fields`, `source`, `source_ref`, `status`, `expires_at`, `quota`, `message`.

Example: dataio auth status --check --json

options.description: Also make one cheap read-only call per provider (10 s timeout) to prove each works.
